Otherwise, this unit completely rocks ~ I purchased it to transfer data via USB 3.0 onto/from micro SDXC cards, and it does that both fabulously and quickly.  I moved 16GB from a 32GB card in just a couple of minutes (literally, a couple of minutes, not twenty+) on my Windows 8.1 machine.  There's no way I could have transferred the same data so quickly using my high-res music player, which isn't USB 3.0. I also like that there is a blue light on the card reader that comes on when it is ready.  The blue light will go off if you insert a second card into the unit concurrently with another, letting you know that the unit is not ready.  If you want a reliable little reader, this is for you, if you're not bothered by the cap issue.

text_fidelity_a:
3DConnexion 3DX-700059 Spacemouse Compact 3D Mouse At first I was skeptical about the idea of using my left hand for this. I was initially expecting it to be a replacement mouse for my right hand, but after more research I understood what they are trying to do. I must say that it's much easier to use than I expected, and operating it with my left hand works just fine.

I was also hesitant because of the price. However, this mouse is fantastic. Worth every penny. I'm using it with SketchUp, and it's vastly easier and faster than the normal built-in navigation tools. It's hard to articulate just how awesome this is. Once you get used to it, it's instinctive and effortless, and moving around the model is so easy! You will absolutely love it.

There was one tricky thing during the setup, however. I plugged it in, loaded the driver, and launched SketchUp. Then I found and opened the configuration window to customize it for SketchUp. The info I had found showed that configuration window with "SketchUp" at the top, and the SketchUp-specific options. But my configuration window didn't have anything specific to SketchUp. It said Windows Explorer at the top instead of SketchUp. I thought I was missing a driver. I messed around a log time, and looked through lots of online info.

At one point, I noticed it said Chrome instead of Windows Explorer. That's when I figured it out. The configuration window changes by itself, based on what application is active. I had SketchUp running in the background, but my most recent activity was with Windows Explorer and then Chrome. With the configuration window open, I clicked over into the SketchUp window, and suddenly the configuration window said SketchUp at the top, and the the SketchUp-specific settings appeared. I wish that had been in the instructions somewhere!!

At first I didn't bother programming the buttons, but later I tried it, and that's an awesome feature. For Sketchup, I programmed one button to be "remove guides", and the other is "paste in place". Hitting those buttons is much faster than finding those things in the menu each time. However, I discovered that I need to make sure I'm not moving through the model when I press the "paste in place" button, or the mouse locks up, and I need to restart SketchUp. But as long as I make sure I'm not moving when I press it, I never have that problem anymore.

Anyway, you will absolutely love this. After using it, I no longer had any doubt about it being worth the money. It's worth every penny. I would give it 6 stars if I could.
text_fidelity_b: 3DConnexion 3DX-700059 Spacemouse Compact 3D Mouse

Canon PowerShot A1400 16.0 MP Digital Camera with 5x Digital Image Stabilized Zoom 28mm Wide-Angle Lens and 720p HD Video Recording (Black) (OLD MODEL) These cameras are amazing. Get a 32GB chip, put CHDK on it and you can do awesome stuff with this camera. I bought two for my family's trip to Alaska, and we snapped thousands of photos. Very good quality, fair low light performance, controls are easy enough. We spent a fair bit of time learning the controls so we'd be fluent with them.

Here's a neat trick: You can use these cameras as low power microscopes. Put the Macro setting on, take a photo as near ask the thing will focus, which is pretty close, then hit 'Play' and use the zoom lever on the shutter release to zoom in and get a microscope view of what you took the photo of.

Also, with CHDK on the SD card, you have a built in intervelometer for taking time lapse sequences.

Another fun thing to do is to take night time photos of the sky using the long exposure setting. With the 10 second setting and the ISO turned up you can capture images of stars or northern lights in the night sky. Fantastic for a $60 camera.

text_fidelity_a:
ZOMEi Tripod, 65" Camera Tripod for Canon Nikon DSLR, Aluminum Alloy Tripod with 360 Degree Ball Head, Professional Tripod for Travel and Work (Orange) This tripod is advertised as 65 inches tall, but that is misleading since you can only reach that height with the center post full extended and somewhat unstable. Most tripods are measured with just the legs and not including the center post or head. This one is about 50 inches tall or 57 inches with the included ball head. You can compare that measurement to other brands.

For a tripod of this height, this one is relatively lightweight and folds up into a compact 20-inch-long case. That makes it very portable for field use. However, they did have to make a lot of compromises in stability to make it this compact and lightweight. The legs have 4 sections (compared to 2 or 3 sections on sturdier tripods) and the thinnest sections are somewhat flexy under moderate weight or in a moderate wind. I don't trust this tripod with a mid-weight SLR camera and exposures of more than 1 second (unless you have the legs folded to half length). For a lightweight camera and fast exposure, this tripod is fine. However, I still would not trust extending the center post in windy conditions, since that amplifies the instability of the tripod legs.

The tripod is attractively finished. I do not like all the twist locks that are slow to operate (compared to cam-locks) and with 4 leg sections, this tripod has lots of twist-locks.

The ball head works OK for this price level and has a quick release plate that also works OK. This company has several different quick release plates sold separately, hopefully one of those will work with this tripod so you can easily use different cameras on it. I have not tried to figure out which one to buy yet, though.

Other people are complaining about the zipper on the case. The zipper on my case broke on the first day of use, too. Just the zipper pull, which is not too expensive to replace.

In summary, this tripod works OK for this price level if you are using a smaller camera and fast exposures. If their goal was to make a lightweight portable tripod, I wish they had made it sturdier and shorter instead of flimsy and taller.
text_fidelity_b: ZOMEi Tripod, 65" Camera Tripod for Canon Nikon DSLR, Aluminum Alloy Tripod with 360 Degree Ball Head, Professional Tripod for Travel and Work (Orange)

text_fidelity_a:
Canon PowerShot SX500 IS 16.0 MP Digital Camera with 30x Wide-Angle Optical Image Stabilized Zoom and 3.0-Inch LCD (Black) (OLD MODEL) I recently took this camera, along with my PowerShot Elph 110, on a Caribbean cruise. Because I have the waterproof case for the 110, I used it whenever I was shooting in wet areas and also for underwater shots. I used the SX500 in dry locations. In some instances, I was able to take comparable shots with both cameras and the difference was really striking. Let me preface this by saying that I'm NOT a photographer. I'm just someone who likes to take a lot of pictures. I like them to come out well, but I know virtually nothing about photography beyond what I've learned through trial and error.

I found the low-light shots taken with the SX500 to be FAR superior than those taken with the Elph. Yes, it's difficult to capture a moving subject in low light. This isn't and expensive, professional camera. I'm very pleased with the results considering the price I paid.

The biggest selling feature was the zoom lens. I was absolutely AMAZED how clear shots taken from VERY far away came out. I took this camera to Opening Day, to see the Red Sox players get their World Series rings. We didn't have the best of seats, so I had to really max out the zoom lens. I was certain the photos would be blurry. It's difficult to hold a camera really still, extremely zoomed in, while standing in a crowd. The photos were OUTSTANDING. I mean really...outstanding!

I'm extremely pleased with this purchase. The camera is small and easy to carry with the strap around my neck. When I want something I can slip in my pocket, I opt for the Elph.

I would classify this as a bridge camera. It's NOT as easy to carry around as a pocket-sized digital, but it's also not as cumbersome to carry around as a more professional model. It's EASY to use...even for novices like me! And it takes great photos. I'm sure as I have more trial-and-error lessons under my belt, my shots will be even better.
text_fidelity_b: Canon PowerShot SX500 IS 16.0 MP Digital Camera with 30x Wide-Angle Optical Image Stabilized Zoom and 3.0-Inch LCD (Black) (OLD MODEL)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony Cyber-shot DSC-WX150 18.2 MP Exmor R CMOS Digital Camera with 10x Optical Zoom and 3.0-inch LCD (Silver) (2012 Model) This is an excellent choice for a camera in this category providing a 10X optical zoom and a variety of useful shooting modes (low light performance is very impressive, so are the panorma sweep, soft skin and background de-focus). It touts the ability to take 3D pictures and underwater capabilities (though I've not tested either). Compared to the pricier [[ASIN:B006K552V6 Sony Cyber-shot DSC-TX66 18.2 MP Exmor R CMOS Digital Camera with 5x Optical Zoom and 3.3-inch OLED (White) (2012 Model)]], this one provides more zoom; however the pricier DSC-TX66 provides a touch-screen control (OLED display) and is much thinner and lighter. The picture and video settings are almost identical for both cameras. Just like other cameras in this family, the battery compartment doesn't inspire much confidence with its flimsy looks.

Having used to the touch-screen controls of TX66, the scroll-based menu in the WX150 seems less impressive - however, the controls on both are very intuitive - given the wide range of options, it will take some time to get used to all the command settings. The video quality of both cameras are exceptional - and either will replace a handycam easily. If you are more interested in a lighter camera with a touch screen and willing to compromise on the zoom (5X opposed to 10X in the WX150) and pay up for it (about 100$ more), DSC-TX66 may be a better choice. But if the touchscreen is not a critical requirement for you and zoom is of more importance, WX150 is a very compelling choice at this price-point. The DSLR-like quality with a very respectable zoom, plethora of picture settings options, and fairly intuitive scroll-based menus makes this a good value.
text_fidelity_b: Sony Cyber-shot DSC-WX150 18.2 MP Exmor R CMOS Digital Camera with 10x Optical Zoom and 3.0-inch LCD (Silver) (2012 Model)

Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote Logitech, Programmable Remote (Silver) What can I say that hasn't been said by 6,200 previous buyers except that this Harmony 650 in silver is a great remote for a small single-remote system.

I'm using it on a patio with a TiVo, a Vizio 40" and an Amazon Basics SB20 sound bar. All three devices were easily found in the Harmony database and entered effortlessly into the remote using the MyHarmony app you download from Logitech to your laptop or desktop computer.

Having used the MyHarmony app to integrate my two Harmony Ultimate hubs for more complex remote IR systems that employ my network/router/phone as interfaces, I was already familiar with how Logitech has set up their software -- so it took only minutes to get the 650 into action.

Hint: before beginning to program your remote, gather the manufacturer and exact model number for each device you are going to control: TV, Amp, Sound Bar, Cable box, DVD player, Blu-ray Player, CD player, whatever. The MyHarmony software will ask you to add all the devices you are going to integrate. You'll need information from as many devices as you have current remotes for. When you're done, you put all the remotes away and use just the 650.

According to the MyHarmony app, the 650 can control 8 devices. I only needed to control three for my patio setup, so it was a simple process.

Bottom line, it's WAY easier to use a single Harmony 650 that to juggle three remotes (TiVo, Sound Bar and TV).

And after just a few minutes of easy online programming that then downloads to the 650 via a USB cable, I'm done.

As the 650 is being used on the patio outdoors, and subject to environmental attack from dust and moisture, I ordered the silicone cover for it. Works great: [[ASIN:B01N2SF2XX Harmony 650 Silicone Case for Logitech Harmony 650 700 Remote Controller Cover Anti Dust Anti-Slip]]
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote Logitech, Programmable Remote (Silver)

text_fidelity_a: HPRT MT800 Wireless Bluetooth Monochrome Portable Printer, Case+Cartridge+Printer，Supports 8.5" X 11" US Letter,Compatible with Android and iOS Phone, No-Ink Technology.(MT800QC) I have always wanted a little printer like this when I was working many years ago but they were never this small.  Now that I go camping in my RV and work while I camp I may want to print something without having to drag a full size printer along for the ride.  The price of this is on the high side even higher than the average full size printer so you better have a need to make it worth it.  Don't do what I did which was to unwrap everything before I ready the manual.  I thought I would have to install the enclosed ribbon but it is already installed at the factory and the one you see is a spare.  I decided to set it up to print from my phone since I mainly use a phone or tablet when on the road.  I downloaded the suggested app and it was easy to get started and I didn't need to sign up or register to do so.  My Bluetooth found it right away.  I selected first to print a photo file and selected low quality as I didn't want to waste ink.  It came out OK.  I next selected a page in a PDF manual that had a [photo embedded in it and selected medium quality and that turned out great.  The only gripe was it only gave me the following places to look for a file to print:  iCloud, Photo, Web and my print history.  I only had a couple things in iCloud as I mainly use Google Drive so I would have to move the document to iCloud first in order to print it.  Photo didn't allow me to browse my photos so I wasn't dure where to go there.  Once I printed a photo inn iCloud then that photo showed up there to print in the future.  I thought that was what the print history was for.  So, the app could use some UI work but I can't complain as everything worked/connected so easily.  Now, the paper.  You have to use their HPRT Premium Multi-Purpose Copy Paper.  It is a bit shiny on one side and more expensive than typical print paper.  This brings me back to you have to really need a niche printer like this to make it worth it.  I cannot sweat these things because I got it to use sparingly while I travel when something just has to be in print form.  I don't even really print much anymore from my home printer so once could say I waste cartridges there.  In summary, if you need a portable printer, that costs more with proprietary paper, for those short run printing emergencies on the road then this is great.  It works great and is easy to setup.
text_fidelity_b: HPRT MT800 Wireless Bluetooth Monochrome Portable Printer, Case+Cartridge+Printer，Supports 8.5" X 11" US Letter,Compatible with Android and iOS Phone, No-Ink Technology.(MT800QC)

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra SUPREME Driver's Edition Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging - Black/Silver I've been resistant for quite some time to using a bluetooth device however recent laws have made it impossible not to have one. And it certainly didn't help hearing friends complain about the problems they had with their bluetooth units.

This is really easy to set up. First you activate the bluetooth on your phone (in my case an Iphone 4), then you open up the Jabra Supreme boom to turn it on and at that point it should automatically enter into a pairing mode with your phone and a blue light will appear on the boom. You should see the device name pop up on your phone as Jabra Supreme, then a voice in your ear will say "connected" and you're set to go. Couldn't be simpler.

It fits very comfortably over my ear even with a baseball cap on and sunglasses. The package also comes with a headphone attachment in case this suits you better. I'm able to hear conversations and respond with total clarity even when I'm driving with the top down in my car. There's also a voice command feature which allows you to redial, call back or activate certain phone commands in a total hands-free environment. And for additional features you can download the available app.

Charging the Jabra Supreme is as simple as either plugging into a USB port or using an AC charger. Battery indicator flashes green while charging and then goes out when it's fully loaded - approximately 2 hours later.

This is a terrific little device. In fact, this may cause me more problems as in the past I was always reluctant to talk on the phone while driving. Not anymore.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra SUPREME Driver's Edition Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging - Black/Silver

text_fidelity_a:
Toshiba TransMemory Pro USB 3.0 Flash Drive (PFU064U-1BDS) With its huge 64GB file storage capacity, this flash drive can theoretically store the entire contents of a PC's hard drive and its operating system. Since I don't have that many files to store on an everyday basis, I am reserving this flash drive to store high-resolution videos and other RAM-eating monster files.

For $80, this is rather overpriced. There are USB drives that are cheaper and will do the job just as well. To make the USB look like it's worth the extra price, Toshiba made the casing unnecessarily oversized - there's no practical reason why the USB case had to be so wide (you will have trouble sticking another USB drive next to it, which is annoying). It's a gimmick to impress the user, nothing more. However, when you hold it in your hand, it's not as heavy as the metallic finish would lead you to believe - it's actually very lightweight, and to be honest, feels cheap. I have questions of its durability, despite the fancy advertising.

To test, I copied all the videos I had stored in my PC to see how fast it would be to store all of them on this monster drive. I was disappointed that the saving time was not noticeably faster, which may not be the fault of the USB drive but rather my computer. However, I have to say it was a relief that I never got the "you don't have enough memory" message, so you can count on this USB to store tons of videos you can't find room for elsewhere.

The only drawback to this single-USB method of storage is that I don't feel entirely comfortable saving so much stuff on just ONE drive, despite its capacity. It's equivalent to putting all your eggs in one basket - what if you lose that single USB - you're screwed. Though convenient, I'd rather spread out my back-up files, so if you use this USB to save a huge file, I'd buy more than one just to be safe.

The other thing I thought was unnecessary was the included encryption software that's included on the drive. You only see it when you open up the Files folder, and there are two lengthy PDFs with instructions on how to activate the password and security options. Fortunately you do not require to activate them in order to use the drive - I've never found I needed such security measures, but if you plan to store financial data on this USB, it's a good feature.

Lastly, I hate the fact that, unlike my other drives, it has a cap. I am forever losing the caps to my flash drives and have since opted to buy only the retractable ones, where you can slide the connector in or out. Too bad this one doesn't have it, otherwise I would have added a star.

So, in short, a mixed review. Give me a drive that's cheaper, that's big on the inside but small on the outside, capless, and I'd buy more of them.
text_fidelity_b: Toshiba TransMemory Pro USB 3.0 Flash Drive (PFU064U-1BDS)

Only issue is the coil whine, which is a roll of the dice. Worst case scenario it'll whine all the time like the first one I tried, whereas my newest replacement only does it during memory tests - which is acceptable.

But other than that, it's excellent. The Carbon and Strix-E both had issues getting my 7200 kit stable at XMP, and I spent almost a week straight tweaking voltages on the Strix - it would always eventually error out in Karhu after 30-60 minutes or so. The Master however is rock solid, and I was able to OC to 7400cl34 with extreme stability. Its "Low Latency/High Bandwidth" options are excellent, and perform better than the XMP tweaked setting on the ASUS.

It also ran the 13900k the coolest, and seemed easier to get stable. Overall if you are lucky enough to not have one with coil whine, it's definitely the best option in this price range.

SanDisk Ultra 32GB UHS-I/Class 10 Micro SDHC Memory Card With Adapter - SDSDQUAN-032G-G4A After I bought this 64 GB micro SD card, I put it in a box with my other SD and micro SD cards until I bought my new phone last year. I installed it with my new phone and SIM card.
Since that time, I have been unable to 'see' the micro SD card, so I could not set it to be used for all the photos and videos that I take with my phone. I connected my phone to my computer and transferred music with no problem since that was stored on my phone's internal memory. I could not download any photos, so I have been having to transfer the photos via my Google photos on my computer. I even removed the micro SD card and inserted it in my card readers and plugged one into a USB port. NOTHING.
So I inserted another micro SD card - this one is 128 GB. VOILA! I was able to see it in my computer as well as in my phone where I was able to access it as well as to format it – finally.

This micro SD card must have been defective from the start, a waste of $35. If I had used it immediately – although I didn't 'need' it at the time, I could have returned it. Now I will find out if the company really guarantees this for 10 years.

Roku Express | Easy High Definition (HD) Streaming Media Player (2018) I received this Roku Express for review, but honestly, I just now installed it and I can't tell any difference between it and my previous Roku Express I got about a year and a half ago. It streams exactly the same as far as I can tell, but it streams very well. It was a bit of a pain to install since the Roku site refused my password and the instructions afterwards aren't all that easy to follow if you lose your password. But, after plugging in all my passwords for internet connection, Netflix, Amazon, etc...it finally started streaming again. I can't tell that it's any faster. Nonetheless, if you don't have a Roku and want to stream a boatload of free channels with movies and lots of other cool stuff to watch, I suggest getting a Roku. You can add paid channels later. And Roku doesn't require a credit card to use.

It comes with a short HDMI cable and everything you need to get streaming. As far as the actual hardware installation, it's extremely easy. It takes less than 10 seconds to put it on top of the TV and connect the 2 cables (HDMI and power). A sticky tape comes to adhere the Roku to the top of the TV since the Roku is so small it tends to fall off with being stuck. This is my 3rd Roku and we rarely watch regular TV anymore.
This Roku will stream in 1080 and 720 psi. I had ordered about 5 or so generic Roku remotes earlier this year since we tend to lose them and one of our dogs has chewed up the original remotes beyond usage, and they all work fine with this Roku.

Roku is always good, just a little bit of a pain to get past all the passwords, codes and stuff in the beginning, especially if your old password for some reason doesn't work anymore.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony Xperia Ear Duo True Wireless headset – Black EDIT: Sony sent me a replacement unit under warranty because of the broken charger. The new unit works as advertised, so I'm upgrading my review to 3 stars. Some users may rate this more highly because of your needs. I give it 3 stars because they are difficult to use, uncomfortable to wear, have mediocre battery life, and are very expensive.

I wanted to give these a fair and thorough test, but unfortunately quality seems to be lacking and it died after just 2 days. First, the rubber ear tip on the right side kept falling off every time I took the earpiece out. Maybe I'm clumsy or maybe it is too fragile, but either way this is really annoying. Second, the battery life is terrible. The battery life indicator dropped from 70% to 30% after just 20 minutes of listening to music. Finally, the charger died. One of the little pins that connected the charger device to the earpiece broke off (or never was attached). Without it, I cannot recharge the right earpiece and since this is a non-standard charger, the whole thing is now useless.

Even if the headphones were 100% functional, here are some general thoughts:
1. Sound quality is very good for headphones that allow you to hear your surroundings. I don't have to take the headphones off to talk to someone standing next to me.
2. That is great because getting these things on or off is much more cumbersome than any other headphone I have ever tried.
3. The user manual really wants you to control these things using finger and head gestures. Maybe my memory is poor, but I can never remember all those things. Even when I'm reading the manual and trying to use the gestures, half the time they don't work.
4. This headset is expensive if all you can do is listen to music and phone calls. They are heavily advertising the "personal assistant" feature as well. The personal assistant feature asks for all kinds of permissions so it can read your messages and emails to you. After the recent Facebook hack, I am really reluctant to grant all these permissions.
5. The personal assistant works best if you have the headphones on all the time instead of just occasionally when you listen to music. However, the advertised battery life of these headphones is only 2-4 hours and my experience is less than that. Constantly recharging these things is a real hassle. Even taking them on and off several times a day is a real hassle.
6. The headphones are cumbersome to take on and off and wear and they are cumbersome entirely because they want to remove the wire between the 2 sides that cheaper headsets have. I don't think that tradeoff is worthwhile if you're not wearing these constantly and you can't wear them constantly because of the battery life.
text_fidelity_b: Sony Xperia Ear Duo True Wireless headset – Black

Logitech Squeezebox Boom All-in-One Network Music Player / Wi-Fi Internet Radio (Discontinued by Manufacturer) The Squeezebox is a radio that you can use to play internet radio, radio services such as Sirius, and music from your hard drive from anywhere in the house.

Setup is quick and easy. You simply install the Squeezebox software and then create a Squeezebox account. The squeezebox account takes seconds to setup. Once you set it up you tell it what radio services you have. I have a Pandora and Sirius Internet Radio account. You enter your login info, and after it verifies it you are setup.

If you do not have any of these, the wizzard will set one up for you. It also works with services such as Rhapsody and Live365.

Using the Squeezebox software you then identify where you music files are located and where your playlist information is located and then that is done.

You then turn on your radio. It automatically connects to your WIFI connection in your home. Using either the control knob on the box or the remote control you can choose your radio services. Within 10 minutes of UPS delivering the box I was listening to Sirius, Pandora, and my iTunes music from my upstairs bedroom.

The sound is great. Truly exceptional with full deep bass and clear crisp tenor and high ranges. Even at low volumes the unit sounds great.

The unit also has a sleep timer, clock, and alarm features. There are several presets to set so you can choose favorite songs or stations quickly and easily.

Pros: Easy setup, works with mac or pc. Uses existing services you probably already have. Wonderful sound, small design.

Cons: The only real con I see is that the unit is a little pricy. Also the menus on the unit take a little getting used to as there are many menus and options nested within each other.

Overall this is truly a wonderful product. Great sound, easy setup, and ease of use. Truly great for audiophiles.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech 3.5 mm Analog Stereo Headset H151 with Boom Microphone - Black, 7.9"x5.7"x2.4" Good crisp audio quality for phone calls. I like an on-the-ear headset instead of in-ear because cell phones have little or no sidetone.

Don't know what sidetone is? Back in the day, land line phone handsets fed the sound from the mic back into the earpiece, so a person could clearly monitor their own voice (and also hear any other sounds that the other party could hear that the mic picked up). That enabled a person to modulate their own voice (instead of screeching in order to hear themselves) and speak much more clearly. It made for a much better phone conversation experience. That feature was called sidetone.

It's a feature that cell phone designers and engineers somehow decided not to add to cell phones, or to make it so low in volume as to be nonexistent.

So until either cell phone engineers put sidetone back into cell phones or headset manufacturers start building it in as a feature, the workaround is on-ear headsets that allow you to hear your own voice while you speak.

The downside is that on-ear headsets aren't exactly convenient to carry around, and they're not inconspicuous. And they can be a bother if you're wearing a hat.

But they do give you some natural sidetone by allowing you to hear the sound of your voice. And this headset from Logitech, as I said, has some good crisp audio quality for phone calls.

Which brings up another point. Even after years of development, possibly the thing cell phones still do worst is make phone calls. The audio can still be garbled and fluttery due to digitizing and signals that fade in and out in strength. So good audio quality---in that mid-range EQ sweet spot---can make cell phone calls a lot more pleasant.

While there's a volume control on the cord, there's no answer button. That's probably a decision to keep the headset compatible with many devices.

Overall, good headset.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech 3.5 mm Analog Stereo Headset H151 with Boom Microphone - Black, 7.9"x5.7"x2.4"

text_fidelity_a:
SiriusXM Onyx Plus Satellite Radio w/ Vehicle Kit, Enjoy SiriusXM Through your Existing Car Stereo for as Low as $5/month + $60 Service Card with Activation So let's start out with that it's a nice step up from your standard car radio. I like the overall design and you can save up to 20 channels and have 5 saved stations that you can tune into to transmit your signal, which I find nice for those areas when you start picking up other radio stations and there is bleed through. I didn't realize this at first, but the radio does have an internal transmitter, though I don't know if having it directly plugged into a transmitter will make any difference. So far mine has done nicely without the help of a third party transmitter. The little screen is nice too. It is not a touch screen, but you can see it well during the daytime and I find that for me the brightness at night is just right, not super blinding bright, but not so dim that you can't see it either. The radio also works similar to DVR and you can rewind to play a song again.

Set up is fairly easy and the instructions are easy to follow as well. I'd say it may take 30 minutes to an hour tops to set it up (that includes tucking away cords and positioning it where you want it) and activating it.

It does not come with a remote, but I think it would improve the experience of going through the channels, especially when driving, so you can still keep your eyes on the road and change the channel if you are wanting something different from your presets. Also, I believe you have to have a Sirius dock/boom box of sorts if you want to bring it inside and play music. You can transfer this radio between cars too, depending on your setup though, you may want to have a secondary dock and antenna set up in the second vehicle so its easier to transition and your not having to drag the dock and accessories around from car to car.

Something to take into consideration if you are thinking of getting this radio or other xm radios is that if you are not familiar with the subscription charges, is that you will have to pay the subscription fee, your state tax and a royalty fee and there is an activation fee. So outside of tax, I didn't realize there were other charges with the subscription fee. Personally I went with the 10.99 subscription and my fees were estimated to be 14.99 (this will probably vary from location to location), so not too much extra on regular fees after the activation fee. Just something to know so your not caught by surprise.

If its really cloudy or if you are under something like a metal awning/covering, the signal will go out.

I think the only thing that I don't like about the radio is the antenna. The reason I don't like the antenna is because the cord is too long for how I use it. I keep the antenna inside my car and the signal works fine, but the cord is ridiculously long. It could be upgraded to a motorcycle antenna, which is about 8 inches long, compared to X amount of feet. For others this won't be a problem, because you may need every bit of that extra cord, so it just depends on how you plan to set it up.
text_fidelity_b: SiriusXM Onyx Plus Satellite Radio w/ Vehicle Kit, Enjoy SiriusXM Through your Existing Car Stereo for as Low as $5/month + $60 Service Card with Activation

I’ve tried using different plug ins for the treadmill and computer, not it (my husband is an electrician and assured me this was not it.). When testing this theory and intentionally removing power and plugging back in, the monitor had a setting box pup-up…. Because it lost powder, great. But when the screen flashes that box doesn’t come up which tells me it’s not loosing power-it’s loosing a connection to the computer. After messing with it and becoming frustrated, I thought I heard a little zap noise where it’s located so when I started feeling around I got a very minor static shock on my finger. So my Inspector Gadget hat told me that I was generating static electricity with my treadmill and for some reason it was collecting on this dual monitor plug and basically shorting itself out. (This only happens when walking on the treadmill.) So, in all my Mom-knowing madness, I wrapped it up in a dryer sheet and it actually works for the most part. It might flash a couple times in a day but my office smells amazing. I will be looking for something else for sure. It’s really annoying.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony XBR75Z9F 75-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart BRAVIA LED TV I really need to begin this review by stating that I am not much of a television watcher - up until this beast was delivered to me a few days ago, and I wanted to sit and experience it before I weighed in. There is not going to be a whole bunch of technical spiel simply because I don't know much about the mighty specs that make this thing cost a fortune, however, when I sit in front of it, I am TRANSFIXED.

I have to tear myself away from the stunning visuals, of which I tested from the mundane to my absolute favorites: regular television shows to the ones that make this a movie theater in your home - watching American Beauty WITH the commentary on so I can be ensorcelled by the teachable moments in cinematography, geeking out on Planet Earth, almost feeling the waves of water, the majestic mountains at your lap, the vivid plumage and wrinkles of parrots and elephants. The elegant clouds soaring through the sky, the dust whirling around in the desert. I am just blown away by how much these images are brought to life with the 4K HD capabilities, and for a TV at this price point the sound BETTER be amazing, which it is. Netflix and Chill will never be the same.

I come home, turn this thing on and feel like Red when he is gliding across the water to meet his dear Andy Dufresne in Shawshank Redemption. I feel like Shug Avery when her father finally welcomes her into the church with open arms. LOL!

There are smart TVs and in this case, this is a genius - once you take it out of the cocoon of careful packaging and set it up, all you have to do is enjoy your apps and Smart Home features like Alexa. Screen mirroring means you can play media right from your phone. Add the Firestick and access any show pretty much from the beginning of time. HDMI connection is a breeze. Football fans will be BLOWN AWAY by the picture quality too, as with any sport.

I don't have anything bad to say - only that I am sad that this thing is SO expensive. So to that end, WATCH OUT for generous discounts as the holidays approach. And even on sale, this TV is so damn incredible that you simply won't have to buy another one for years. Put that way, this is worth three dollars a day over the course of those years for something you will not ever experience elsewhere from Sony's top of the line. This Master's series is truly masterful.

I was fortunate enough in that this model worked perfectly for me right out of the box and was astonished to read about the other viewer's experience, and do hope that this review of a WORKING model will help. I'm looking at the cheaper Sony models for a television for my bedroom and will be watching those sales myself. I'm so thankful to have been able to receive this because I am turned on AND plugged in in a way that I really had no idea was possible!
text_fidelity_b: Sony XBR75Z9F 75-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart BRAVIA LED TV

SmartDelux 13-Port Powered USB Hub = 10 USB 3.0 Data + 3 Charging Ports for PC & Laptop, 5ft PA Cord UPDATE (5/19/2019):
Today my external hard drive is not recognized when it is plugged into this hub. I am NOT restarting my computer to test whether it is necessary to have the HDD recognized. It IS recognized when it is plugged into a different hub that is also plugged into my Mac mini.

Since my 4-bay HDD enclosure has to remain connected for the hourly Time Machine backups, it is now connected directly to my Mac mini. The only reason to keep this hub is for charging any device.

UPDATE (2/15/2019):
Other drives (SSD and HDD) that were connected to this hub also disconnected themselves. The wired Apple aluminum keyboard (it came with my 2008 Mac Pro) is plugged into this hub, and it does not generate the warning that the device was disconnected. If I were shopping for a USB hub, I would stay away from this one. Nothing is "deluxe" except the name - and the lighted ports.

UPDATE (2/9/2019):
My devices - SSDs and 4-bay HDD enclosure - that are plugged into this hub have been disconnecting for no apparent reason. I thought my Logitech mouse was disconnecting because the dongle was plugged into it, but that seems to be the fault of the dongle since it continued while plugged into my keyboard. I have moved my keyboard cable to the hub, and we will see how long that lasts. The 4-bay enclosure is more critical, so it is connected to a USB port on my computer. When the enclosure was connected to this hub, I kept seeing that warning that my drives were Not Ejected Properly

Connected this to my computer's USB 3.0 port. Plugged in the dongle for my battery powered mouse. Mouse began acting erratically, had to remove the dongle and reinsert it to reconnect. Functioned properly for a short while but disconnected.
Finally had to plug dongle in the port on my wired keyboard before it would stay connected and not perform erratically. Something must be interrupting the signal even when the LEDs indicate the hub is connected even during periods when my computer is asleep.

ORIGINAL REVIEW (1/25/2019):
The hub has 3 smart charging ports, but when viewed from an angle, only the two on the end have orange / red LED light showing - the 3rd one appears blue. All lights are bright - brighter than they need to be.

A 4-bay HDD enclosure is plugged into this hub and has been functioning without any problem for the 2 weeks I have had the enclosure connected. Connecting an SSD through this hub also functions with no problem using a SATA-USB3 cable.

Jabra Engage 65 Wireless Headset, Stereo – Telephone Headset with Industry-Leading Wireless Performance, Advanced Noise-Cancelling Microphone, Call Center Headset with All Day Battery Life,Black This is a moderately high-end headset with a price to match. The manufacturer claims that it supports multiple devices at the same time, that it has a long range of 490 feet, that the battery charge lasts "all day," which most of us would interpret as 8-12 hours or more, and that it has a noise-cancelling microphone and enhanced speakers to create "crystal-clear calls" in noisy work environments.

I have tried to pair it to both my phone and TV transmitter at the same time, and the TV transmitter does pair if the phone is paired. The range isn't as far as advertised. The battery charge lasts about 4-6 hours. It has excellent sound quality for receiving calls and listening to TV, but persons on the other end of a phone call often complain that they have trouble hearing me, so the mic doesn't work very well. This headset is really uncomfortable to wear, making it difficult to use it more than an hour. Also, be aware that the rechargeable battery is not replaceable when it dies.

I actually have a headset with similar functions that cost me about 1/5th the price, so I'm not convinced this product is worth the extra money.

I can be in our small house and he can conduct his business privately. Definitely a plus. Music sounds great, everything sounds great. Have not use them for calls.

Overall ... these are worth the price. Best part is how they fit and stay in my ears. I would not hesitate to recommend these to someone and I, for one, have no regrets.

Asus Dual-Band Wireless-N600 Gigabit Router (RT-N56U) This router is very good in terms of speed and signal strength, it is better than the Cisco E4200 v.1. However I was also interested in the ability to backup to USB attached drives. The E4200 does a much better job, actually the RT-N56U fails miserably when trying to backup using Windows backup to a USB drive (NTFS or FAT32). It seems they do not have plans to make this work in the future.

Unfortunately their customer service do not offer too much help.

Following you will find how they answered a question I submitted regarding the USB attached drives issue:

My question:
I have been trying to use Windows Backup with a drive attached via USB to this unit. I
have tried different hard drives formatted both as FAT32 and NTFS. Backups always
fail. Mostly with Error code: 0x80070008. Is there a compatibility issue between this
router and Windows Backup? I still have two weeks to return this router if I cannot
make it work.

Their response:
The router has its own settings that will operate reguardless if the computer works or not. The computer has nothing to do with the router software one way or the other. If you need to back up the router setting then I suggest you take screen shots of the router to verify that you can save the settings from there.
Thanks Aaron Asus Support Team

Well, I am still trying to figure out what their response means...

Do not get this router if you need USB features. They do not work.

I'll just compare this one to the pink one in terms of what's different.

I like the black color of this, the ability to put it on a keychain or lanyard, and how small it is, but I don't like the way it all handles nearly as much as I do the [[ASIN:B0168C6MB4 16 GB player]] that I will review separately. The controls and settings are just awfully fiddly and not terribly intuitive. That you can add up to 16GB extra memory via an SDHC card (for a total of 24GB) is a boon, and that's the only thing I like better about this player than the 16GB one; the latter does not have an expansion slot. It's a useful thing if using a player like this when exercising if you can swap out different kinds of music for different types of activity—what works for running or walking will be different than what you'd use for swimming or dancing, for example. But still, these players all hold a decent amount of music natively, and you can also copy a ton of files to it if you're using it to double as a flash drive.

Here's the original functional review for this type of player:

The first thing I tried was the FM radio, because I was really doubtful it was going to work very well in my bedroom, but I was able to pull in NPR and the voices were crystal-clear. The earphones that come with this look really cheap, but they sound pretty good. As with any earphones, they don't cancel surrounding sounds, which makes them perfect for going out for a nice brisk walk. I actually prefer earphones to earbuds because earbuds never fit my ears right. These are like the original Apple earphones, and they stay in my smaller ears really well. I think it's a nice touch that these earphones are included with the player because you can use them in situations where you don't want your really good headphones to get lose or ruined. The device has the following menus, accessible by pressing the Menu button, then the right play button to cycle through them.

SETUP: It's very fiddly trying to set these settings. It takes a lot of trial and error to get it all to work. These are the settings: Clock, LCD Set (not sure what this is), Language (came set to English), Power Off (I can't figure out how to get into these settings to set the times to zero so the player doesn't shut off too soon, so this is why I'm knocking it back to three stars), an Online Mode, Firmware Upgrades, Memory Info.

MUSIC: Navigating through music is straightforward cycling through folders and files. I set up a Walking Songs folder and also dragged my whole Collective Soul Folder with Subfolders to the device, and I was able to navigate between the folders before playing. Selecting specific songs is more difficult. I've never learned how to create playlist files (I know, I know), so I can't say if those will work. There is a funky little equalizer animation on the screen when you play a song.

VIDEO: There's actually a nice music video included on the device, and it will play over and over if you don't stop it. I can see that this might make it possible to put together a loop of items to keep a child entertained on a trip, but it might also have utility for studying, memory work, a flash-card-like experience, or the like.

RECORDER: What it is. Records in .wav format at 32kbps. Great for quick reminders or embarrassing your friends.

VOICE: Used to play back recordings.

FM RADIO: Works great on the stations I've tried, without an antenna of any kind. I may have to start listening to more radio while I'm working.

PHOTO: A simple photo viewer, so you can keep all the pictures of your pets or kids that you'd normally have in your wallet to inflict on the people you meet. I'm just learning about QR codes (scanned my first one on my phone the other day), but I would think you could generate QR codes to carry on this device as well. The device does not recognize .png or .eps files, but it reads .jpgs fine, even larger ones (which do take a bit more time to load).

EBOOK: This is for reading simple .txt files. Don't think you can put anything proprietary like Kindle ebooks on it; it didn't read the .mobi file I copied onto it, or the .epub, or the .pdf. But who'd want to read a whole big book on such a tiny screen anyway? Use the EBOOK capability to take grocery lists or short paragraphs of instructions with you.

GAMES: I almost forgot the games. I'm not a game player. There are a handful of games that I haven't bothered to look at.

This player is not a super-fancy high-end piece of electronics, but it's a lot of bang for the buck and also something you wouldn't die over if you happened to lose it. Of course, you can always use it instead of a flash drive to take files with you different places for subsequent transfer. So it's a lot of functionality in one small package.
text_fidelity_b: G.G.Martinsen Crystal-faceted 8 GB Mini Usb Port Multi-lingual Selection 1.8 LCD Mp3/Mp4, Video Player, Music Player, Media Player, Video player, Audio player With a Slot for a micro SD card--Black

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech USB Headset Stereo H650e This is a decent, serviceable headset but rather expensive for the price. I have another Logitech headset for home use but this one was definitely better in quality.

Appearance: the plastic casing feels a little cheap, which raises questions about its durability. I once owned a Sharper Image headphone that had a similar feel, and it broke after a year or so.

Function: the headphone is lightweight and quite comfortable to wear, thanks to the padding on the top and the ear muffs. However, the muffs are thinner than I expected. For the price, I would have liked them to be thicker and offer better noise cancellation capabilities. The microphone, however, feels professional grade, being bendable and sensitive. In addition, the long cord is very work-friendly - it's thicker than conventional cords (preventing easy tangling) and long enough for me to reach over my desk without concern that it'll tug or pop out. Also convenient are the location of the controls for volume, phone and speaker - they're on a rectangular box located on the cord itself. Cool.

However, setting up the headphone took some work. With my other Logitech headphone, all I had to do was plug it into the USB drive, let the computer recognize the device, and off I went. Here, I had to be patient and follow the specific setting instructions for Windows 8. Listening to videos and audio files worked fine, but the microphone function didn't work when my phone rang and I tried ti answer using the mike. I pressed the button but nothing happened. As it turns out, the phone function appears to work only when you're hooked up to Linc, an application that nobody in my office uses. The instructions didn't make this clear.

The sound quality is decent for business purposes but for hi-fidelity sound, it's average. I had assumed it was a noise cancelling headphone because of the padding, but I was wrong - I had no trouble hearing some of my coworkers bickering a few feet away while I was listening to a webinar. I had to up the volume to block them out.

The headphones come with a smooth zippered vinyl pouch for storage or for traveling. This was a very nice touch.

Overall this is a decent enough headphone for work but I would have given it five stars had the price been lower.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech USB Headset Stereo H650e

text_fidelity_a:
NIXGIR UNL A1 True Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.3 Headphones with ENC Microphone, HiFi Stereo Sound, 18H Playtime, IPX4 Waterproof Okay, so price to satisfaction ratio is one way to define the products' quality. It is really not expensive yet not so excellent either. So here is what I think.

Build Quality / Design: it's small and very conventional Bluetooth earbuds design, so looks very similar to Air Pods. Build quality is not so bad for its price and I have no complain about this part. The matt brushed finish does look pretty fancy but I don't know why they leaved some part unbrushed. So some part looks pretty nice but some look like just plastic. Yet, since it is $14, so I don't think I should complain so much.

Sound Quality : I am not so sure about this part. This does have all the functions which earbuds should have (touch control, voice calling etc) but it simply lacks the depth of the sound. It sounds like slightly improved version of Air plane bundle earphone, so not worth to discuss about base/mid/high range. For sound quality, something is off in the sound quality.

Ergonomics: So this one has old Air Pods design, you cannot change the soft rubber to adjust the size to fit your years. After few hours of use, I felt uncomfortableness and slight pain with this ear phone but I have small ear and I feel pain with Air Pods as well, so my opinion is not so important for this matter I guess.

Buy if you are looking for : some quick substitute for your Galaxy Buds / Air Pods / or other ear buds and price is very important for your purchase decision. Interestingly, this earbuds mic is weirdly good.

Don't if you are looking for : earbuds with excellent sound quality / very comfortable fit
text_fidelity_b: NIXGIR UNL A1 True Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.3 Headphones with ENC Microphone, HiFi Stereo Sound, 18H Playtime, IPX4 Waterproof

text_fidelity_a:
ZyXEL 300 Mbps Wireless N Access Point, Ethernet Client, Universal Repeater, and Range Extender (WAP3205) Overall this is a good little feature-rich device but use just the wireless access point features. It was quick to setup but was definitely a time that you wanted to read the fine manual (RTFM (PG version)). It wasn't as easy to setup as the CISCO WES610N that I purchased at the same time BUT it is also feature rich.

I have had it up for a few days and haven't experienced major problems with it. We will see if it stands up to the test of time and gives me 3-4 years of service like my Cisco Linksys devices that are still working 4 1/2 years later.

Nerd Alert - I am a nerd at heart and utilize geek speak way too often. I try to remember that the Amazon audience contains friends, family, and strangers that may or may not know IT.

PROS:
* Feature Rich -
The ZyXEL is 1/2 the price of the comparable Cisco device but it has a much more feature rich set of wireless capabilities. It supports WPS, allowing for easy setup. It supports WDS, allowing you to configure a network that allows you to carry your laptop from room to room in a large house without sacrificing much speed if setup correctly. It can access as a repeater if needed.

* Cabling -
The ZyXEL includes the power supply and a network cable (CAT-5). It supports a standard called MDI/MDIX, which means that you won't need a crossover cable if you connect it to a switch.
* Wireless Distribution Service -
You can make this part of your existing network using WDS, or Wireless Distribution Service, or simply configure it as an access point. I just removed two old Linksys routers from being WDS nodes since replacing my old Actiontec 802.11a/b/g with an Actiontec 802.11b/g/n wireless router. Eventually I will get around to using the ONI port and setting up a network with DD-WRT

CONS:
* LAN ports on the back are are 10/100 -
While the router notes that it supports connection speeds up to 300MbPS it only has two (2) 10MbPS/100MbPS RJ-45 (LAN) connections. Technically you may never truly realize the full throughput available with this device. This is not unlike other wireless access points, such as the Cisco WET610N (single 10/100) or the Cisco WES610N (quad port 10/100 for $10 more). I did what any good geek would do; used it as an excuse to purchase an 8-port Netgear 10/100/1000 switch to replace my 5-port 10/100 switch in my office/lab with the computers and Hyper-V lab systems. I am going to use the Cisco product downstairs with my home server and VMWare ESXi box.

* Setup may be difficult for the average home user -
I most certainly RTFM'd and reading the manual helped. It did take a quick configuration of my network card in order to even get to the point I could setup the device.
The Cisco devices use an APIPA address, which makes setup easier. Why? APIPA is that 169.254.#.# address that your computer gets when it connects to a network that doesn't give out addresses. This allows you to easily setup the Cisco WES610N.
text_fidelity_b: ZyXEL 300 Mbps Wireless N Access Point, Ethernet Client, Universal Repeater, and Range Extender (WAP3205)

For those of us w/ a LOT of media, Plex is the pinnacle of enjoying your own media with the best interface possible (and it's free); whereas KODI is the best way for streaming media from the internet. The Shield recognized my old archives instantly, and also when I plugged in a USB3 SanDisk flash drive for extra space. I've had 3 WDTVs, 2 Nexus Players, and 1 MiBox, and I wasted all of that time and money until I got this. I've KODI Phoenix and Exodus for internet streaming, and Plex for my 200 movies, 25 seasons of TV shows, 75 instructional videos (on guitar, magic, and yoga), 6k songs, and all my family albums and artwork. I have the Plex client (player) for TV, phones/tablets, XBox 360, Chromebooks, and Chromebox.

The Shield has BOTH the Play Store and the NVidia Store on its dashboard. I can play all my games again because this console doesn't stutter and freeze up. I'd missed my Asphalt 8 when the others just couldn't handle the workload anymore. I can get even better games from the NVidia Store that the Play Sore doesn't have. Of course, all previous purchases come right back to the Shield --like the HomeRun HD. Plex has a deal they're making w/ HomeRun HD to possibly turn the shield into also doing DVR.

The gamepad has been totally redesigned and has gone from an Ugly Duckling to being prettier than a pail full of kittens. The hex-grip feels good in the hand for shooting zombies or driving on racetracks. The gamepad is rechargeable (yay!) and even comes w/ it's own charging cable. The once $50-extra remote is now included w/ the console. Like the gamepad, the remote also has a headphone jack for discreet listening and a touchscreen volume control and Mute.

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra Elite 7 Active True Wireless— Bluetooth Sports Earbuds Shake Grip for Secure in-Ear Fit — Ultimate Workout Earbuds, Adjustable Active Noise Cancellation, Fast Charging — Navy Whoever designed the packaging for this had some fun with it. Opening it all is an interesting experience, in a good way. On the box, it says "thoughtfully designed, purposely engineered, expertly built" I think for the most part, they live up to it. Something tells me they pay their product designers well.

As usual for earbuds, they're hard to pry out of the magnetic case. The case does have a charging light on the front. It's so tiny, you probably won't see it until you plug it in. It's bright despite being the size of a grain of sand. Easy to see, which is nice. Easy to cover if it's by your bed. The case is small, smooth, and well built. More pocket size than most such charging cases.

I tried on the earbuds and the fit is ideal for me, and I've tried about seven brands. As soon as I put them in, they started giving me instructions on how to pair them.

I was irritated to find that the instructions tell me to install an app to get further instructions and functionality. This is typically where things fail, and I was primarily wanting these for a Windows tablet, not my phone, but I gave it a shot. The app does indeed give further instructions on how to use them, and also updated the firmware with no fuss the second time I opened it, complete with flashing purple LED on the case. The app also has a bunch of adjustments to the level of noise cancellation, equalizers, many soundscapes, like rain and pink noise, that work well with the cancellation to block out the world. The button functions can also be rearranged, which is nice because every brand seems to be different, and it's nice to be able to switch it to something personally intuitive.

I ended up connecting them to both my tablet and my phone, and now when I put them on, they say, "two devices connected" If I'm playing audio on my tablet, and then pause it and play audio on my phone, it seamlessly plays whichever is running, though not both at once. I like that I should be able to listen to my tablet and then take an incoming call. I'm not an audiophile, but the sound quality seems excellent to me. I've tried a couple expensive brands with noise cancellation, and it's interesting. It doesn't remove background noise very effectively, but it does a bit. I think it's more that when it's turned off, they use the mic to pump in outside audio so it's almost like you aren't wearing them. Neither mode is especially effective, so I wouldn't buy them for that specifically, but It's a small benefit. It's best suited for making your audio your focus or your situational awareness your focus.

I tried them on a call and it went well. My first time using earbuds for a phone call, and I have no complaints.

Definitely my new favorite earbuds, and I've got pricier ones. So far price has had little impact on my earbud opinions, mostly because design is still so much more variable and important than quality. I've only got two notable criticisms. One, every set I try is harder than the last to pry out of the case. Magnets are great. So is a sleek look to everything. Give us a divot in the case where we can get a finger under the edge. The other problem is range. Range is average, but when I tried walking out of range, instead of announcing the problem and handling it, they just cut out and turned off. I had to actually put them back in the case before they would go back to playing.

Overall, even with a few minor quibbles, these have become my new favorite earbuds, after having about seven (from good brands) in my family's stash to try. They fit well, audio quality is very good, the app actually functions and they are just a very solid, comfortable offering.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Elite 7 Active True Wireless— Bluetooth Sports Earbuds Shake Grip for Secure in-Ear Fit — Ultimate Workout Earbuds, Adjustable Active Noise Cancellation, Fast Charging — Navy

SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers For an apartment with only one door and one window that opens this set is great. But most places need a few more. For a dorm room this is fine. I've only seen dorm rooms that had one door and usually the dorm rooms windows are several stories up so it would probably be pretty hard for someone to enter that way. Unless it's on the ground floor.

The door stop alarm is extremely LOUD. And it will not stop SCREAMING until it is physically switched off. This is the first of this type I have ever tried out. A few years ago I bought about 10 door stop alarms of another brand and they were also very loud. However, once the pressure plate was released back up they would stop screaming. I guess it's good that it continues to scream until you stop it. Especially in a dorm type living situation. Someone would eventually come to see what was the matter. It takes one 9 volt battery.

The window alarm is extremely simple to install and the double sided sticky tape that comes with it is very strong. I have several of these window alarms attached to various windows at my home. They aren't the loudest but they should get the job done of scaring off an unwanted intruder. It takes 4 LR44 button batteries.

The personal key chain alarm is o.k. It's got a loud scream that makes my ears ring. It takes a good tug to pull out the pin to activate it. The small LED light is better than no light at all but don't expect a bright beam. It will help you find your keys if you dropped them in the dark. I think along with a sincere scream for help and the personal alarm screaming as well, I would think most aggressors would give up and try for an easier target.......at least I would hope so. It takes 3 LR44 button batteries.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Sense 2 Advanced Health and Fitness Smartwatch with Tools to Manage Stress and Sleep, ECG App, SpO2, 24/7 Heart Rate and GPS, Shadow Grey/Graphite, One Size (S & L Bands Included) At this point, I have had the Sense 2 for 2 days and I know at least some of my issues will likely be fixed with later software updates. First, the good. I like the form factor. The case is thin and the watch, even with the supplied band, is comfortable. Speaking of the band, as a big guy, I was overjoyed to see the inclusion of a second band that actually fit. Also, changing bands is a snap.

Overall, it seems to be relatively high quality. The battery life, so far at least has been fantastic. I am on hour 42 of wearing it after a 99% charge and it is down to 70% battery left. The screen is fairly bright and crisp. An understated advantage of the Sense 2 (and one of the reasons I switched) is that is OS and phone brand agnostic. You can use it with Apple or Android and, unlike the Galaxy Watch, there are no features locked away if you are not using the correct brand of phone.

If you are coming from a Galaxy Watch where you could customize the watch face and all sorts of other things and that is important to you, then move along. This watch will not be for you. For now, at least, there is not really much substantive you can do to individualize your user experience. That's not so great.

Also not so great is the things that are missing. There is no Google Maps at launch. Also, despite being a Google company, no support for the Google Assistant (Alexa only sadly). There is also no interface to control music on your phone if that is important to you. I found it mildly annoying, but not a deal breaker. In addition, some people will be turned off by the fact that there are features that require a Fitbit paid subscription to get, even though you get six months for free.

The real reason I bought this watch was the ECG function. I have had A Fib for a couple of years and used to use (and still do) a Kardia XL to check my rhythm. The Galaxy Watch 4 was nice because it did a reasonable single lead reading and it meant not having to carry another gizmo with me. You simply held still and put a finger on each of the side buttons. Unfortunately, when I switched from a Galaxy phone to a Pixel, I lost the ability to do an ECG.

On the Sense 2, the ECG has not been impressive. First, I have big hands and contorting my right one to get my thumb and forefinger on the corner of the glass has been a challenge at time. It often takes several tries to get it right. Second, despite confirming on both my Kardia and my Galaxy Watch, the Sense 2 will never indicate that I am in A Fib. Apparently, if your pulse goes above 120 (which mine frequently does while in A Fib) then the Sense 2 just gives up and won't really check. Even in instances where it was below 120, the Sense will not confirm. I guess we get to settle for inconclusive results instead. Given this feature was the main reason I bought the watch, it may be a deal breaker for me and I may return it for that reason. If this feature is not that important to you, then it may still be a good option.

Overall though, it may be a good option for the right person. If you care primarily about health and fitness tracking and want a good battery life, then this is a good option. At the current $300 price point, I still feel like Fitbit may be asking a little too much given the features of the other higher end options on the market.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Sense 2 Advanced Health and Fitness Smartwatch with Tools to Manage Stress and Sleep, ECG App, SpO2, 24/7 Heart Rate and GPS, Shadow Grey/Graphite, One Size (S & L Bands Included)

text_fidelity_a:
Altec Lansing VS2620 Speakers for Computers and MP3 Players (Black) I was initially surprised when I unpacked these speakers because they were a lot larger than I'd expected. In fact, I think they're rather large for laptop speakers unless your laptop doesn't travel the way mine does, around the house or outside of it. You're not going to be carting these speakers along with you. They'll probably end up as speakers for my desktop.

Portability issues aside, they do provide good sound for their size and price point. Tone is crisp and clear, and while you can't do much more than play with the volume and brighten or darken the sound, you can still do some reasonable fine-tuning here. I'm sure there are audiophiles out there who will disagree with me, but then I don't really think that listening to music or watching DVDs on your computer provides optimal enjoyment no matter how good your speakers. It's a convenience, not worth selling your firstborn for.

Apart from the size, my only other quibble is that here is yet another piece of equipment that I have to find a plug for, and a plug that will accommodate yet another bulky transformer. I realize that external speakers which operate on juice from the computer are probably pretty sad little things, and that it's a trade-off, but I really am getting tired of all those black blocks.

But the bottom line is this: I'm sitting here listening to Pandora Radio and it sounds good to me for a change. The sort of good that would get me back to listening on a regular basis. And that, my friends, is the real test of these speakers and their relationship to my laptop. They may not end up attached to the desktop after all.
text_fidelity_b: Altec Lansing VS2620 Speakers for Computers and MP3 Players (Black)

I did ditch the stock cable for a 1.5M SKS because I don’t require the 12’ cable that came with the cans, although it’s a nice cable. I do see a headphone amp in my future, perhaps the Little Bear B-4X portable tube amp. Lord save me from this addiction 😀

10 Inch Tablet, 64GB Storage Tablets, Android 11 Tab, 512GB Expandable, 8MP+2MP Camera, 1.5Ghz CPU Quad-Core Processor, 2GB RAM WiFi 6000mAh Battery, 10.1'' HD 1280*800 IPS Touch Screen Google Tablet I was one of the FIRST people to own an iPad back when they were introduced. It was a birthday gift. And, I honestly regret giving up a trip to Disneyland for it. Yes, I had a choice between what I thought was going to be a lifelong, productive item for a trip to Disneyland.

I did go to Disneyland in 2015 though, so I was a few years late. Regrets? Should’ve taken the trip and NOT gotten the iPad. It barely works today (can’t upgrade the iOS due to NOT having a camera – a front facing one for some updates). And, I have it in my desk drawer. REALLY PEEVED at Apple for that one.

So, I’ve been REAL hesitant to jump on the eReader or tablet train. They upgrade, change, and modify so fast. Honestly, I use my iPhone for certain things while I use my laptop. The rest? I use my laptop. I don’t really read eBooks to justify an eReader, nor do I like it. [I did try it with this – still a no go – clunky, awkward, no “book smell”, and so easy to lose my place.]

Seeing this? I decided to grab it. After all, I USED to be a Samsung Galaxy (Android) user. I had to replace my GS8 and the iPhone I was had a cheaper plan through my carrier. No regrets there. But, I still remember the Android system. My mom still has her GS8 phone, so I HAVE to know it.

Looking at the price, around $60 (as of this review) – this is a basic, no frills tablet. It is a “no-name” brand, but that doesn’t mean much. I’ve had trouble with numerous brand name items, so name doesn’t matter.

Now, this is VERY SLOW. Even a cheap Acer laptop can be slow. My mom had one and the language … hello? Content warning!!

This is, to me, great for pre-teens and teens. It’s not too expensive that parents will really scream if something happens (like say an iPad or more expensive $100+ tablet). Or, it can work for someone who wants some internet functionality, and wants to read eBooks. The Kindle app works great here, just not my style.

I can check my email accounts – Outlook and Gmail – no real issues. I’ve ordered fast-food. As far as games? The one I tried didn’t work (Hogwarts Mystery)

As far as a user manual – like most devices nowadays (or the ones I’ve bought in the last 5-8 years) – the MANUAL (instructions) are on the device, usually a PDF. This was the same for the last three HP laptops I bought in 2010, 2011, and 2019. And, it was the same for the last two phones (GS8 and iPhone 11). Also, my iPods in 2008 and 2013. So, yes, I do have a LOT of experience with the lack of a physical manual. The manual can be accessed by swiping the homescreen UP. It is a PDF file.

There are some apps that ARE NOT COMPATIBLE with this device, even if you have them on a Galaxy phone. These can range from productivity to fast food. IE: Tropical Smoothie Café’s app is compatible, Taco Bell isn’t. My bank’s app isn’t compatible, but I can access the website through the Chrome browser (which I also have on my iPhone).

However, a GIANT bonus for me – MICROSOFT 365. I was able to add WORD to the tablet, and since I have cloud storage – ALL MY DOCUMENTS are AVAILABLE to view and edit.

Overall – this is, as I stated: a BASIC or STARTER tablet. Better suited for ages 8 to 15. I say this based on the fact that at 8, I would be able to care for this, and use it. By 15, I’d likely save up my allowance for a higher priced tablet or get it as a gift.

I am pretty pleased with it, and will likely use it for several things.

Monoprice Active Indoor/Outdoor HD6 HDTV Antenna, 50 Mile Range, Video Antenna (115953) Black Before you buy, check the Monoprice website for this item. The price may be much cheaper over there.

This is a very inexpensive, relatively low quality TV antenna. You get what you pay for. They advertise this for both indoor and outdoor use, but the mostly plastic construction will not last long outdoors in areas that get a lot of wind, ice, or bright sunlight. The attached 3 foot cable really tells you what their intended use case is. If your TV is near a window, hang the antenna in the window, plug it in, and you're done.

The advertised 50 mile range is for ideal conditions, mounting the antenna outdoors in an area where there are absolutely no obstructions between your home and the TV broadcast tower (no trees, no buildings, etc). Expect much worse range for an indoor mounting and if there are any obstructions. If you live in an area with trees etc, you should get a more sturdy antenna that can be mounted on a pole on top of your roof so it can receive a signal over the trees.

This antenna is advertised for UHF frequencies only. Most TV stations use UHF these days, but in my area there are a couple that use VHF and this antenna is not usable for those channels. If you really want VHF, I suggest getting a different antenna from this one.
text_fidelity_b: Monoprice Active Indoor/Outdoor HD6 HDTV Antenna, 50 Mile Range, Video Antenna (115953) Black

text_fidelity_a:
Fantom GreenDrive 500 GB USB 2.0/eSATA Desktop External Hard Drive with 2 Year Warranty GD500EU Firstly, let me say that, being a closet tech-geek. I have owned countless hard drives over the last two decades. I own stock in Seagate, so I purchased [[ASIN:B000ND75C0 Seagate FreeAgent 500 GB 3.5-Inch USB 2.0 Hard Drive ST305004FDA1E1-RK]], (only the 1TB version) from them and, to my dismay, it just stopped responding to power after a couple of months (I got it working, but it was a let-down for sure with the stock thing and all). Then, I ordered this really, really expensive, crappy paperweight here: [[ASIN:B006Y5UV4A WD My Passport 1TB Portable External Hard Drive Storage USB 3.0 Black]] (same basic drive, just an earlier model no longer offered, I think), and was ready to use it for skeet practice in no time. I hated that I needed to use their software to access the data on the drive. As for the actual software, it was a total PITA. But it didn't matter because, within weeks, the damned thing crashed for good--and I wasn't even doing anything weird with it. :|

So, about three years ago, I stumbled upon the Fantom Greendrive and was, at first, kind of put-off by the apparent size (it's actually not as big as the Seagate, it turns out). I really wanted something small and portable. But, after all those issues with other drives, I really, REALLY wanted something RELIABLE. I first did some research, took a chance and ordered this drive.

DEAR GOD. IT IS MARVELOUS.

That was, as I've said, three years ago. Three years of constant use: heavy data transfer, being knocked around (even dropped on the ground a couple of times), never defragged (I got lazy cos' it's so reliable), never disk-checked, numerous power-loss and disconnection incidents....nothing can kill it! It hums along nicely no matter what you throw its way.

You don't have to ever worry about unmounting it before you turn off the power--you just unplug it and go. It's never failed me and, to be honest, that makes it better than one particular husband, in my book (the second is doing quite nicely, thank you).

The "Green" is for:

---Firstly, it doesn't take a lot of power. Nice.

---Secondly, despite being dropped a few times, it hums nicely and quietly. No loud grinding at all. I always have to check to see if it's on (which is easy because a green light shines through the grate of the front to let you know the power is on).

---Thirdly, if you have it plugged in but haven't accessed it in a while (like fifteen minutes), it will initiate a semi-hibernation, then go into a bit of a deeper hibernation after like a half hour or so (never timed it, but it's cool when it does it). So if you hear a click and a sound like the motor is clicking off, that's what you're hearing. Cooler still, the minute you click to access the drive it's ready to go--little to no wait.

It's also very fast. As drives go, mine is almost full and THREE YEARS OLD and, like I said, never defragged, yet it still runs faster for data transfer than my brand new laptop...which makes me wonder about my laptop. ;/

I actually love this drive so much, I figured with my bad luck, one day it's finally going to give up on me and quit for good. So, about a year ago I purchased the newer 2TB drive[[ASIN:B002XITVCA Micronet Technology Fantom GreenDrive 2 TB USB 2.0/eSATA Desktop External Hard Drive GD2000EUS]]for more space and extra backup. I love having the two of them because, unlike many products, Fantom keeps the peripherals consistent, so the power supplies (though upgraded to a one-piece rather than two-piece on the newer model) are interchangeable, as are the USB cables (though the 2TB, being newer, is obviously a 3.0 rather than a 2.0). Still, transferring data between the two is easy-cheesy and fast.

So, all in all, I have to tell you that, despite being an incurable tech-geek, this drive is honestly the best, most reliable, and durable piece of electronics equipment I've EVER owned.
text_fidelity_b: Fantom GreenDrive 500 GB USB 2.0/eSATA Desktop External Hard Drive with 2 Year Warranty GD500EU
